headline: High-risk workspace and data-flow overlap: Cline can write/egress broadly while cognee handles personal/finance data, creating default leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, so it can ingest content that may be attacker-controlled; cognee stores and processes documents and workflow data, so its outputs could be bridged back into Cline through shared files or APIs. The pair has a plausible shared-channel pathway, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Cline consumes cognee-generated files or MCP outputs as instructions, injection becomes active.
IF both agents share a workspace directory, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of cognee outputs as prompts.
Separate workspaces per agent.
Require explicit human review before Cline acts on any cognee-produced text.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only sources.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad network egress and handles browser screenshots plus workspace files, while cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If they share files or a workspace, Cline can transmit sensitive content to its model provider or external sites by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF Cline is pointed at the same workspace as cognee, sensitive files can flow into Cline's context.
IF Cline's browser or model provider is used on cognee data, that data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts.
Block Cline from opening cognee data folders.
Redact personal and finance data before handoff.
Disable browser access on sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; cognee has session memory and allowlisted egress. Their overlapping access to mutable project artifacts creates a write-conflict pathway, especially if both operate on the same repo or data store without locking.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or database, concurrent writes can collide.
IF no external lock is present, one agent can overwrite the other's state.
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths.
Pause one agent during the other's write phase.
Use git branches per agent.
Add a manual lock file before edits.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived content, and cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If cognee treats Cline's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into stored memory and later reuse. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF cognee ingests Cline output without validation, incorrect facts can persist.
IF Cline's browser-derived content is stored as workflow memory, downstream actions may amplify errors.
mitigations: Require source citations before ingestion.
Add a human approval step for stored memories.
Mark browser-derived outputs as untrusted.
Limit cognee writes to a staging area.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before persistence.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Cline handles browser screenshots and workspace files with broad egress. If EU or regulated data is processed through Cline, the pair can create residency and retention mismatches; Cline's docs-only profile does not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed from cognee into Cline, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the agents, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cline.
Use a DPA-reviewed deployment path.
Minimize retention in both systems.
Document data residency for each agent.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and audit logging.
